mappings.note: Separates economic from non-economic activity - the chapter's central distinction. CG-SST4 is the goal about the socio-economic role of institutions such as the market; its only outcome, LO-297, covers occupations rather than this classification.
Illustrates economic activity through a shopkeeper, lawyer, driver and factory worker: named occupations (LO-297) within the economic frame (CG-SST4).
Why community service is prized though unpaid - seva, langars, cleanliness drives: contributions of sections of society (CG-SST4) resting on the value of seva (LO-300).
The forms compensation takes - wage, salary, fee, payment in kind; the working of the market, so CG-SST4.
Anu and Kabir noticing how varied everyone's work is - the chapter's opening survey of occupations (LO-297) as economic life (CG-SST4).
Geeta Aunty as an Air Force pilot; a named occupation, so LO-297 rather than the general economic outcome.
Kabir's grandfather giving free Geography lessons after retiring - an unpaid contribution to the neighbourhood, so CG-SST4 and not LO-297, since no paid occupation is involved.
Anu's parents running a uniform shop; a named occupation, hence LO-297.
Anu's mother volunteering to teach knitting - an unpaid contribution, so CG-SST4 rather than the occupations outcome.
Defines economic activities as those done for money or money's worth; the core definition of the chapter's economic frame.
'Fee' as payment for a professional service - one of the forms of compensation in the market, so CG-SST4.
Asks what 'money's worth' means. The printed answer is lost to page furniture, but the question is a clean market-vocabulary item, so CG-SST4.
A damaged duplicate of the money's-worth item whose supplied answer is about payment in kind; either way the content is the forms of compensation, so CG-SST4.
Salary as a fixed monthly payment against a wage reckoned hourly or daily - a distinction between forms of compensation, hence CG-SST4.
Picks the one genuinely economic activity from four, with the free-teaching options as distractors; the economic/non-economic classification, so CG-SST4.
A clothes-collection drive classed as non-economic community service; the same classification demand, under CG-SST4.
A new highway cutting travel time: infrastructure provided by government (LO-294) delivering a wider economic benefit (CG-SST4). Not LO-297, since no occupation is at issue.
The grandfather's post-retirement teaching, gardening and errands - unpaid but valuable work, so CG-SST4.
'Money's worth' as an equivalent monetary benefit in an exchange; market vocabulary, hence CG-SST4.
Finds 'salary - payment for volunteer work' false among market, fee and wage: all four options are terms of the economic frame, so CG-SST4.
A damaged duplicate whose supplied answer is that charging a fee for online classes makes the teaching economic; still the economic/non-economic classification, so CG-SST4.
Defines a wage through Sahil the farm labourer: a form of compensation (CG-SST4) attached to a named rural occupation (LO-297).
Payment in kind, exemplified by Sahil's mangoes - a non-cash form of compensation, so CG-SST4.
Rajesh the carpenter's 600-to-1,000 rupee margin read as value added by his skill: the market concept (CG-SST4) worked through a named craft occupation (LO-297).
A doctor's paid consultation against free treatment of family or friends: the classification (CG-SST4) applied to one profession (LO-297).
Caring for a sick grandparent classed as non-economic; the classification demand again, so CG-SST4.
Seva as selfless service in temples, gurudwaras, mosques and churches - a value of India's older traditions (LO-300) driving unpaid work (CG-SST4).
The langar as seva in practice: a traditional value (LO-300) expressed as service to the whole community (CG-SST4).
Swachh Bharat Abhiyan as a national campaign built on citizen effort: collective unpaid work (CG-SST4) alongside a government mission (LO-294).
Van Mahotsav tree planting raising awareness of forests - community participation in unpaid work, so CG-SST4.
Festival organising valued for the bonds it builds rather than any earnings; the worth of non-economic activity, hence CG-SST4.
Rohan the software engineer drawing a monthly salary: a named urban occupation (LO-297) and its form of pay (CG-SST4).
Sorts farmer, mother, lawyer and volunteer into economic and non-economic and settles on the lawyer's fee: the classification (CG-SST4) across named occupations (LO-297).
A street vendor selling fruit in a market - an urban occupation (LO-297) that is plainly economic (CG-SST4).
Non-economic work adding nothing to the money economy yet being vital to well-being; the chapter's central evaluative claim, so CG-SST4.
Finds the wrongly classified case - the knitting volunteer called economic - across the chapter's cast; the classification demand, so CG-SST4.
Keeps only the carpenter's sale as economic, ruling out cleaning one's own house and a free health camp; again the classification, hence CG-SST4.
Meera's salaried teaching set against her unpaid weekend storytelling: the classification applied to one person's two kinds of work, so CG-SST4.
Names the value-addition process by which raw materials gain worth at each stage - a market concept, so CG-SST4.
Rajesh's labour and skill adding monetary value to wood: the value-addition idea (CG-SST4) through a named craft occupation (LO-297), like the earlier carpenter item.
